The given equation is \(\tan 53^\circ \tan 81^\circ \tan x^\circ = \tan 53^\circ + \tan 81^\circ + \tan x^\circ\). This matches the form of the tangent addition identity: if \(A + B + C = 180^\circ\), then \(\tan A + \tan B + \tan C = \tan A \tan B \tan C\). More generally, the equation is equivalent to \(\tan(53^\circ + 81^\circ + x^\circ) = 0\), provided the tangents are defined and the denominator is non-zero.

Set \(53^\circ + 81^\circ + x^\circ = 180^\circ \cdot k\) for integer \(k\). Since \(0 < x < 180\), the sum \(134^\circ + x\) lies strictly between \(134^\circ\) and \(314^\circ\). The only multiple of \(180^\circ\) in this interval is \(180^\circ\). Thus \(134^\circ + x = 180^\circ\), giving \(x = 46^\circ\). Checking the denominator confirms it is non-zero, so the solution is valid.

Answer: 46
